title: Consumer sovereignty
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:14Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-markets-answer-economic-questions, covers what, how and who get goods in a market, so it is broader than the single consumer-sovereignty idea, and the other two points are about consumer guarantees and ethics, which are different ideas.

draft.title: Consumer sovereignty
card: Consumer sovereignty means consumers have the power to decide what is produced. They do this through what they choose to buy and what they leave on the shelf.
When many people buy a product, sales rise. Businesses see this and may make more of it, or make similar products.
When people stop buying a product, sales fall. A business that ignores this loses sales and may need to change what it makes or stop making it.
This works in a free market, where businesses are free to choose what to make and consumers are free to choose what to buy.
draft.remember: Consumers vote with their spending, and businesses that ignore them lose sales.

a.q: Which situation best shows consumer sovereignty?
opts: Shoppers stop buying a snack, so the maker changes it
A maker adds a new snack and tells shoppers to buy it
A snack maker lowers its costs by using cheaper packaging
A snack maker advertises more than its rivals do
a.why: Consumer sovereignty means buyers' choices steer what is made. Here shoppers stop buying, and the maker responds. In the option where the maker simply tells shoppers what to buy, the business is leading, not the consumers.
a.clue: Who is steering the choice about what gets made?

b.q: Leo runs a bakery in Ballarat. He keeps making a loaf that fewer customers buy each month, while customers keep asking for sourdough. What is most likely to happen to his bakery?
opts: It loses sales to bakeries that make what customers want
It keeps its sales, because Leo chooses what is made
It gains sales, because the loaf is now rarer
It is forced to close within a month
b.why: Customers choose where to spend, so a business that ignores their wants can lose sales to rivals. Leo does choose what to bake, but that does not protect his sales. Losing sales does not mean the bakery must close at once, so the closing option goes too far.
b.clue: Customers can take their money to another bakery.

a.best: Shoppers stop buying a snack, so the maker changes it

b.best: It loses sales to bakeries that make what customers want
